slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Harlow should fix promotions, shrink and delivery and exit weak stores, not cut store hours
Promotions, shrink and delivery drove the decline; store labor explains only 13% of it
–	Gross margin and e-commerce fulfillment explain 79% of the fall from 3.37% to 1.02%
–	Wages rose 9.4%, but productivity held labor's rise to 0.3 percentage points of sales
The draft 8% hour cut could net only $4.5M of its $14.5M saving once shrink rises
–	The thinnest-staffed stores lose 3.1% of sales to shrink, against 2.3% in the best-staffed
Resetting promotions, fixing shrink and growing private label add about $19M a year
–	38% of FY2025 promotional events lost money, yet price perception worsened
–	Promotions back to 24% of sales add $10.5M, the largest single action
E-commerce loses about $10M a year in full; the tested delivery fee cuts that by $2.8M
–	Only 30% of online sales are new to Harlow, and the reported 6.1% margin omits delivery
Six actions reach a 3.1% margin; promotions, the delivery fee and shrink start first
–	The first three actions lift operating income to about $33M, above the $20M covenant
–	The board is asked to approve three long-lease exits, at $7.5M of the $25M limit

slides.title: Promotions and shrink, both within Harlow's control, explain the whole fall in gross margin since FY2023

paragraphs.text: 1 Diagnosis    2 Labor    3 Gross margin    4 E-commerce    5 Plan
Promotions and shrink, both within Harlow's control, explain the whole fall in gross margin since FY2023
Change in gross margin by driver, percentage points of sales, FY2023 to FY2025
Each driver has an operating cause Harlow can act on
▪	Promotional mix: promoted sales rose from 24.0% to 29.0% of sales, and each dollar earns 14 percentage points less margin
▪	Less vendor support: suppliers funded 46% of markdowns in FY2025, down from 55%, so Harlow carries more of each event
▪	Shrink: up from 2.1% to 2.6% of sales while hours per $1,000 of sales fell (section 2)
▪	Private-label mix: share up from 17.0% to 18.5% of sales at 12 percentage points more margin, the one driver working for Harlow
1  Effect = change in share of sales × margin gap (promotions 14 pp, private label 12 pp); shrink counts 1:1. Together the three equal the 1.02 pp fall in gross margin
2  Source: Harlow Fresh Markets briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis (Tables 1 and 2)
Sources: Harlow Fresh Markets briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis

slides.title: Thinly staffed stores already lose the most to shrink: 3.1% of sales, against 2.3% in the best-staffed quartile

paragraphs.text: 1 Diagnosis    2 Labor    3 Gross margin    4 E-commerce    5 Plan
Thinly staffed stores already lose the most to shrink: 3.1% of sales, against 2.3% in the best-staffed quartile
Shrink, % of sales, FY2025, stores in quartiles by labor hours per $1,000 of sales
Fewer hours mean skipped checks on fresh food
▪	Fewest hours (Q1): these stores lose 35% more of their sales to shrink than the best-staffed quartile
▪	Why: their managers say produce rotation and receiving checks are skipped on busy days
▪	Exposed: fresh and produce waste (45%) and receiving errors (20%) make up 65% of shrink, both tied to staff time
▪	Over time: chain hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6.0% in FY2023–25 while shrink rose from 2.1% to 2.6% of sales

slides.title: The draft hour cut could net as little as $4.5M of its $14.5M saving once higher shrink is counted

paragraphs.text: 1 Diagnosis    2 Labor    3 Gross margin    4 E-commerce    5 Plan
The draft hour cut could net as little as $4.5M of its $14.5M saving once higher shrink is counted
Draft 8% cut in scheduled store hours, $ millions a year, at FY2025 sales
saving a year, management's estimate
more shrink a year: 0.67 percentage points of sales if shrink tracks hours as in FY2023–25
net saving a year, before lost sales from checkout waits or stock-outs
Four assumptions; the first makes this an upper bound on the shrink effect

▪	Shrink responds to hours as it did in FY2023–25, when hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6.0% and shrink rose 0.5 percentage points; all of that rise is put down to staffing, which makes this an upper bound
▪	The saving is management's estimate of $14.5M a year, close to 8% of FY2025 store labor of $181.9M
▪	Sales stay at the FY2025 level of $1,503M
▪	Lost sales from longer checkout waits and stock-outs are not counted; they would lower the net saving further
A cut treats a minor cause of the decline and feeds a major one: move hours to the high-shrink stores instead

slides.title: Rolling out the tested delivery fee would cut the e-commerce loss by about $2.8M a year and keep home delivery

paragraphs.text: 1 Diagnosis    2 Labor    3 Gross margin    4 E-commerce    5 Plan
Rolling out the tested delivery fee would cut the e-commerce loss by about $2.8M a year and keep home delivery
$7.99 fee and $100 free-delivery threshold, chain-wide, $ thousands a year, at FY2025 volumes
more fee income: 703k delivered orders at $6.40, against 772k at $3.10
less delivery cost: 9% fewer delivered orders at $13.80
more picking as click-and-collect orders rise 14%
contribution lost on 2% lower online sales
gain a year; the loss falls to about $7.6M
The test was small, so the rollout should be staged and tracked
▪	The 4-store, 10-week test holds chain-wide: delivered orders −9%, click-and-collect +14%, online sales −2%, fee $6.40
▪	Costs per order stay at FY2025 rates; the provider's proposed 3% rise would cost about $0.3M a year
▪	Lost online sales follow the survey: 70% move to Harlow stores and 30% leave Harlow
▪	Delivery still loses money: about $9.04 per delivered order at the tested fee, against $1.64 for click-and-collect
Use the contract renewal to resist the 3% rate rise: the fee alone does not make delivery pay
1  Estimate by the team from the fee test (4 stores, 10 weeks, late FY2025). Source: Harlow Fresh Markets briefing pack (synthetic data); team analysis (Table 5)
